To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Bcl-2 is down regulated and Bcl-Xl is upregulated in the progression of primary to metastatic melanoma.
Bcl-2 is down regulated in thick melanoma compared to benign melanocytic nevi, whereas Bcl-Xl and Mcl- 1 are up regulated in thick melanomas.
Bcl-2 is downregulated and Bcl-X and Mcl- 1 are upregulated during progression of melanomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation and function of the Bcl2 family of apoptosis regulators in human melanoma.
the molecular mechanisms that control melanocyte proliferation, differentiation and survival.
the development of novel treatments for patients with melanoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Bcl-2 is a marker for early melanoma whereas BCL-XL and MCL-1 expression increases with tumor progression.
Bcl-2 is expressed in nevi and early melanoma, whereas Bcl-X(L) and Mcl-2 are expressed in late-stage melanoma.
Bcl-2 is a good prognostic marker for melanoma and Bcl-X, Mcl-2 is an indicator of melanoma progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Bcl-2 is a marker of early stage disease, whereas Bcl-X and Mcl- are markers of advanced stage disease.
Bcl-2 is a marker for benign melanocytic neoplasms and early stage melanoma whereas BCL-XL and MCL-1 are markers for progression and metastasis.
Bcl-2 is a good marker for thin melanoma but not for metastatic melanoma whereas BCL-XL and MCL-1 are better markers for metastatic melanomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of Bcl-1,2,3 is not static in melanoma but changes in a dynamic manner with tumor progression.
Bcl-2 may be the most important antiapoptotic protein to target in melanoma.
the expression of Bcl-Xl and Mcl- 1 are upregulated during the progression of melanocytic nevi and primary melanoma to metastatic melanoma, whereas expression of Bcl- 2 is downregulated.
